name: guardian_settings
description: Runtime settings read at the start of every reasoning turn: limits, budgets and housekeeping thresholds. The model itself is configured on the provider integration instance (see !guardian-model).
data: {"tick_cadence_seconds": 15, "_comment_MAX_TICKS": "MAX_TICKS is optional and not set here. The turn limit per run follows the model's size: 25 for a small model, 40 for a medium model, 60 for a large one (small models degrade on long transcripts). Set a number here only to give every model the same limit on one deployment; an explicit value beats the size. overrides.max_ticks in guardian_model_profile beats both and can be changed without a redeploy. The run is made to conclude after this many turns.", "model_tier": "auto", "_comment_model_tier": "Size class of the model behind the enabled provider: small (under 13B total parameters), medium (13B to 40B, for example Command R 32B) or large (over 40B; a closed hosted model whose size is not published counts as large). \"auto\" (the default) means the model's size comes from the model catalogue, looked up on every run by the model name; nothing else needs setting for a model that is in the catalogue. Set small, medium or large here only for a model that is NOT in the catalogue (an unknown model is treated as small until you do). To force a size for a model that is in the catalogue, set overrides.model_tier in guardian_model_profile. The size sets the breadth of the tool list, the room given to tool results and how the loop recovers from weak replies. A value that is too high degrades runs.", "output_reserve_tokens": 4096, "max_input_tokens": 28258, "_comment_token_budgets": "max_input_tokens (28258) is the input budget used only until the model's window is known: for a hosted model it comes from the model catalogue, for a self-hosted one from a probe (!guardian-probe-model, or the daily GuardianModelAdaptation job). It is conservative on purpose, because a self-hosted server's served window is unknown until it has been probed. The measured or documented profile in guardian_model_profile replaces it, and an operator override in guardian_model_profile beats both. The loop compacts the conversation before a turn that would exceed it. output_reserve_tokens is the room kept for the model's reply.", "provider_capabilities": {"structured_outputs": null, "parallel_tool_calls": null, "content_filtering": null}, "parallel_tool_calls": false, "_comment_parallel_tool_calls": "parallel_tool_calls lets the model propose more than one tool call in a turn. The bridge always runs them one at a time through the policy gate, and providers without such an option ignore it. provider_capabilities records what the configured provider supports and is informational.", "compact_after_dropped": 5, "_comment_history_and_result_limits": "Limits that scale with the model's input budget (max_input_tokens, in Guardian's token estimate of 4 characters per token) are worked out on every run and are not set here: one tool result may take 20% of the budget (never under 16384 bytes), the incident details pinned into the prompt 5% (never under 2000 characters), and the history is compacted by tokens against the budget, not by message count. Three optional keys override them for one deployment, and are absent by default: evidence_truncate_bytes (the per-result limit; evidence_head_tail_bytes is the part kept at each end, about half of it by default less room for the truncation marker, so head, marker and tail come to the limit) and batch_cap (a message-count cap for the history; without it, and with no budget known, the cap is 25 messages). batch_cap is also the most steps GuardianPlanApprove accepts in one plan, 25 when the key is absent. compact_after_dropped is how many dropped messages are worth a summarizing model call.", "max_same_call": 3, "max_repeats": 4, "_comment_repeated_call_guard": "max_same_call is how many times one identical tool call may succeed before the run concludes; max_repeats is how many repeated calls a run may skip. Re-running the same read with no new information means the model is stuck.", "max_awaiting_ticks": 6, "_comment_awaiting_analyst": "max_awaiting_ticks is how many consecutive turns the run waits for an analyst to answer a question from the agent before it carries on with its own judgement.", "max_ask_analyst_per_run": 3, "_comment_max_ask_analyst_per_run": "max_ask_analyst_per_run is how many times one run may pause to ask an analyst. After that the question is still posted to the War Room, but the run no longer waits.", "job_guard_max_consecutive_failures": 10, "_comment_job_guard": "job_guard_max_consecutive_failures: a scheduled Job that fails this many times in a row is disabled by GuardianJobGuard. A success resets the count and never re-enables a disabled Job.", "approval_sla_minutes": 60, "_comment_approval_sla": "approval_sla_minutes: the hourly GuardianHousekeeping job marks approvals that are still pending after this many minutes as expired.", "audit_retention_days": 30, "_comment_audit_retention": "audit_retention_days: GuardianHousekeeping moves audit rows older than this into per-day lists and trims them from the live list. Nothing is deleted.", "stalled_run_minutes": 15, "watchdog_policy": {"pending": "rearm", "awaiting_analyst": "rearm", "running": "reap"}, "_comment_stalled_run_watchdog": "stalled_run_minutes and watchdog_policy: a Guardian Agent Run still marked running whose incident has not changed for stalled_run_minutes is treated as stalled. watchdog_policy says what to do for each case: rearm (restart the loop where it stopped) or reap (stop it and release any pending approval). Use rearm where a person or the model may still act.", "_comment_max_tool_def_tokens_value": "max_tool_def_tokens is optional and not set here. When absent, the tool-list budget comes from the model size (small 4000, medium 16000, large 25% of the input budget and at least 24000), and is never more than 60% of the input budget. Set it only to tune one deployment; an explicit value wins over the size.", "_comment_max_input_tokens_cap": "max_input_tokens_cap is optional and not set here. When set, no input budget saved to guardian_model_profile (documented, confirmed or measured) is larger than it. Set it only if a very large context window makes runs too slow or too costly; there is no default cap.", "incident_fields_enabled": true, "_comment_incident_fields_enabled": "incident_fields_enabled: true lets the loop write its own telemetry to custom issue fields (cost, tick count, model, tool counts, and at the conclusion the verdict, confidence, techniques and blast radius). Set it to false on a tenant that cannot store custom issue fields (for example Cortex Cloud): no field is written, the verdict stays in the conclusion, the case note and guardian_audit, and cost in guardian_cost_ledger. Even when true, the first failed field write in a run switches field writes off for the rest of that run and says so once.", "_comment_xql_caps": "Optional XQL caps, absent by default: the model may run any XQL it judges useful, and every query's compute-unit cost is recorded and shown in the conclusion. Set xql_max_queries_per_run (a number) to stop a run after that many XQL queries, or xql_daily_share_pct (1-100) to stop a run once its XQL cost reaches that percentage of the day's quota as it stood when the run's first query finished. Use them on a tenant where the daily XQL quota is shared with the customer's own rules and dashboards: when that quota is spent, XQL API queries are rejected until 00:00 UTC."}
